dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, yes. Um, I know it's after five-thirty, City Hall is closed, I got the storm line off the recording. So I hope somebody's actually there.
I'm here. This line stays open for storm and drainage issues after hours. What's going on?

Okay. It's about the parking lot behind my building. It's on Marsh Street, three, three, eight Marsh Street, down the Point. The lot in back slopes toward the back door, and every time we get a real storm the water runs right down and floods the entrance.
Three thirty-eight Marsh Street, in the Point. And the water comes from the parking lot toward the back door?

Yes. The drain in the lot, it's, it's just not taking anything. After last weekend's nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday, there was a pond at the back door. Still a lot of standing water on Monday. It keeps happening and nobody ever fixes it.
I'm sorry, that sounds like a headache. Is the water getting inside the building, or is it at the doorway?

It's at the doorway, it's up to the threshold. Um, we put towels and a board down. But people have to walk through it to get in. And the other thing, the cars. People cut through that lot to get around the traffic on the street, and now everything is slowing to a crawl through the water. Everybody's creeping, there's a wave, it's a mess.

So the traffic is slowing down going through the flooded part of the lot. Let me make sure I have this right. The lot behind three thirty-eight Marsh, the storm drain there is not draining, and the water pools at the back entrance.
Right. Exactly. And I have called, well, I've mentioned it before to the landlord, and he says it's the city's drain. So.

Okay. I can't tell you offhand whether that particular drain is city-owned or on the private lot. I'll write it up for the drainage crew to look at, and they can determine that. Is the drain visibly clogged, with leaves or trash on top of it?
Um, there's a grate. [pause] It's got leaves and, and sand, and I think some gravel piled on it. I can't tell how deep it is. It's slow, even when it's not storming, a puddle stays for days.
That's helpful. Debris on the grate and a puddle that lingers. Is there anywhere else nearby that's flooding, or just that lot?
The street out front gets wet at the corner, but that's, you know, that always gets wet. It's the back lot that's the problem for us. The back door.
Got it. I'll note the lot specifically. And what's the best number to reach you if the crew has questions?
Okay. It's four, zero, one. [pause] Five, five, five. [pause] Zero, one, six, three.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-six-three. Did I get that right?
Yes, that's right. Thank you.
And your name for the ticket?
Marisol Pagan. P-A-G-A-N.
Marisol Pagan, got it. I'll put it in tonight, and it goes to the crew supervisor in the morning.
Okay. Can I ask something? Do the crews work weekends? Because if it floods again Saturday, I don't want to wait until Monday for somebody to look.

They do respond to emergencies on weekends, and after a big storm they're out there. For a standing-water drain issue like this, though, it's usually handled on a regular work day. If it gets really bad, you can call this line again and tell us it's blocking an entrance.

Okay. I'm not trying to be difficult. It's just I'm going to be out tomorrow morning, I'm chaperoning a class trip to a farm, forty fourth graders, so I won't be here if anyone shows up. And my phone will be, who knows, in a barn.
Understood. I'll add a note that you may not pick up tomorrow, and that they can leave a voicemail. Would somebody else at the building be able to point them to the lot?
Maybe the upstairs neighbor. I'll ask. But you can tell them it's the lot behind the building, the one with the grate near the back door.
I'll put that in exactly. Lot behind three thirty-eight Marsh, grate near the back door, debris on top, water running to the entrance, vehicles slowing through it. Anything else I should add?
Just that it's every storm. Every one. I'm tired of calling about it.
I hear you. I've got it all written down, and I'll flag that it's a repeat problem. You should hear from someone in the next day or two.
Okay. Thank you, Lorraine. I appreciate you picking up this late.
Anytime. Have a good night, Ms. Pagan.
You too. Bye.
